title: Offline Install Bundle Playbook — air-gapped mirror & upgrade checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects notes for building an "offline install bundle" workflow for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Focus: artifact mirroring, packaging dependency bundles, Terraform module expectations, and a repeatable upgrade path for air-gapped environments. Draft / working notes — lots of TODOs and questions.

Audience:
- Solutions engineers and infra SREs preparing customer air-gapped installs
- Release engineers building offline bundles and upgrade artifacts
- Platform engineers updating Terraform modules for private deployments

High-level goals:
- Produce a single deployable artifact directory that can be transferred offline (USB / air-gapped host / internal transfer service) to customer environment.
- Bundle everything required to install, verify, and upgrade Redwood Private (control plane + runtime) without outbound internet.
- Make Terraform changes idempotent; allow operators to re-run modules after transfer.
- Provide clear upgrade plan with preflight checks, step ordering, and rollback guidance.

Contents of offline bundle (proposed):
1) OCI images tarballs (docker save style) for:
   - runtime images (inference runtime, api gateway, sidecars)
   - observability collectors (otel, prom exporters)
   - nginx/traefik variants used in chart
2) Helm charts (packaged .tgz) and values patches for air-gapped use (chartmuseum optional)
3) OCI/Helm index + signed manifest + sha256 checksums + detached signatures (cosign)
4) Terraform module versions + provider plugin binaries (if needed for offline) OR exact provider plugin checksums + install instructions
5) OS packages and local package repo snapshot (deb/rpm) for required packages: containerd, runc, iproute2, jq, etc.
6) Language packages: python wheels / pip cache for python deps used by operator tooling and admission controllers
7) GPU drivers + CUDA/CUDNN bundles (if customer uses GPUs) with exact matching driver install scripts and verification tests (nvidia-smi test images)
8) Init scripts and systemd units for pre-install host prep (iptables sysctl, kernel modules)
9) A small registry proxy container that can be run locally to act as an offline registry (Harbor flat-file archive or registry:2 tarball + preloaded images)
10) Post-install validation scripts & sample workloads (LLM sanity checks, latency smoke tests)
11) Upgrade bundles (delta tarballs + migration checklist)
12) Readme + troubleshooting + known issues

Packaging rules / naming convention (work-in-progress):
- bundle-v{major}.{minor}.{patch}-{release-tag}.tar.gz (e.g., bundle-v1.4.0-20241130.tar.gz)
- inside: /images/, /charts/, /packages/, /terraform/, /scripts/, /signatures/, /manifests/
- manifest.json (small index) that lists all artifacts and checksums — signed

Terraform module notes (what the modules must support for offline installs):
- module should accept image_override_map (map of imageName -> localRegistry:tag) and skip_remote_lookup boolean.
- provider installation: document approach for local provider plugin installation (for TF < 0.13 plugin behavior) — we prefer using terraform init -plugin-dir but must include plugin binaries in bundle and verify OS/arch.
- state backend: support for filesystem backend for initial brings (local state file) with clear migration instructions to s3-compatible backends after install.
- idempotency: modules must tolerate re-apply after partial installs; use resource meta-arguments where possible (create_before_destroy)
- version pins: modules must pin to exact module version and provider constraints inside bundle manifest.
- hooks: pre_apply hook script and post_apply verification script that operators can run in offline environment.

Terraform offline checklist (notes for devs):
- Build process: terraform init --get-plugins=false? Not possible. Concrete flow we trialed: include provider binaries + set TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR env at runtime. Need to test across terraform versions (1.4, 1.5).
- Provide a small helper script (tf-offline-wrapper.sh) that sets TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR to ./terraform/plugins and runs terraform init/apply.
- Include example tfvars for customer envs (cidr ranges, vip addresses).
- Document how to move from local file state to remote state (s3/consul) if customer later allows connectivity.

Registry & image mirroring notes:
- Two supported offline registry formats:
  a) Preloaded single-host registry tar (registry:2 + /var/lib/registry content).
  b) An OCIR/Harbor export — preferable where allowed.
- For simplicity start with approach (a) for supported customers. Provide small Docker Compose that boots registry:2 and pushes images using skopeo copy from tar.
- Use skopeo to convert between docker-archive -> oci-archive -> docker registry. Include skopeo binary or static build in bundle.
- Tag rewrite strategy: image_override_map used by Helm/Terraform to point to local registry. Provide sed/values transforms.
- Signed manifests: cosign sign manifest.json and include cosign public key in bundle for verification.

Dependency bundle specifics (OS / drivers / language):
- Debian/Ubuntu: apt-mirror snapshot .deb collection + Packages.gz + release file (gpg signed). Repository can be served by a simple nginx instance included in bundle.
- RHEL/CentOS: create local yum repo with createrepo_c; include rpm packages and repodata.
- Python: wheelhouse built with pip wheel --wheel-dir. Provide pip.conf to point to local file:// wheelhouse.
- Node: tarball of node_modules? prefer shipping yarn offline cache + npm package tarballs.

GPU & driver concerns:
- Critical to include strict mapping of kernel versions -> driver versions. Provide a small matrix file.
- Include sample driver install scripts for: ubuntu-20.04, ubuntu-22.04, rhel8. Scripts must be idempotent: check existing driver version before reinstall.
- Licensing note: drivers are subject to vendor license; ensure customer has rights to transfer driver binaries. Document in README.

Upgrade plan (example v1.3 -> v1.4):
1) Preflight (offline): check bundle manifest signature, verify checksums, ensure disk space, verify kernels and package versions.
2) Backup: export current manifests, export control-plane DB snapshot (if applicable) to offline bundle storage.
3) Load artifacts into local registry and local package repo.
4) Run terraform plan (offline wrapper) to compute changes. Review plan carefully — highlight any destructive ops.
5) Apply operator-controlled upgrades in order: infra (LB, storage) -> control plane -> runtime nodes -> agents.
6) Post-upgrade integrity tests: smoke LLM endpoints, run perf sample, verify KV cache warm-up.
7) Rollback plan: prefer blue/green where possible. If not possible, restore DB snapshot + reapply previous tfstate and restart images from previous tag.

Preflight & validation scripts (todo list):
- check-space.sh: disk and inode checks
- check-kernel-compat.sh: verify kernel vs driver matrix
- check-tf-plugins.sh: verify provider plugin binaries available and checksums match
- check-images.sh: verify image tarballs readable and matches digests in manifest
- smoke-test.sh: start a minimal cluster and run end-to-end call to /health endpoints

Operational pitfall notes (real-world things we've seen):
- Mismatched container runtimes: customers sometimes use docker vs containerd; our images assume containerd. Need compatibility notes & small helper for docker->containerd transition or include cri-diff adapter.
- SELinux and AppArmor differences cause unexpected pod failures. Include clear guidance to set policies or disable for install window.
- Time drift: cosign verification can fail if system clock is wildly off. Add note to sync ntp before verification.
- Customer proxies blocking signature verification or cosign key retrieval — always include public key in bundle.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we include terraform binary in bundle (and which versions)? Security implications.
- How to handle large model shards? (models are out of scope for core platform bundle but customers often want sample models offline). Maybe provide a mechanism to register external model store after runtime is up.
- Decide on standard offline registry approach (registry tar vs Harbor export) — propose documentation for both but make registry:2 tar the minimal supported path.
- Legal: confirm redistribution rights for closed-source OS packages and GPU drivers for our bundled delivery. Ask Legal (ticket JIRA-PD-1273).

Notes to self / reminders:
- Coordinate with release-engineering for reproducible bundle creation pipeline (CI job that outputs signed bundle tar.gz).
- Add automated checksum generation and cosign signing step. Use ephemeral key per release and rotate.
- Build a small acceptance test runner that can run locally against extracted bundle (CI step).

References / links (internal):
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PRIVDEP-4821 (air-gap playbook parent)
- Jira: JIRA-PD-1273 (legal check for driver redistribution)
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/56 (initial offline bundle prototype)

Last notes:
This is intentionally rough. The aim is to converge on a minimal supported offline bundle that is easy for SEs to deliver and for customer engineers to apply. Next steps: prototype a bundle with registry:2 tar + helm charts + terraform offline wrapper and run it against an ubuntu 22.04 VM (virtual lab).

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Marco: build first-pass bundle prototype and upload to internal staging (due 2024-11-17)
- Priya: draft terraform-offline-wrapper.sh and provider plugin packaging guide (due 2024-11-24)
- Jonas: create kernel-driver matrix and sample gpu install scripts (due 2024-11-20)
- Aisha: coordinate legal review and sign-off + update this doc with final packaging rules (due 2024-12-06)

END OF DRAFT
